findings.claim: `touched` and `dirty` are not input props of Base UI `Field.Root` (they are read-only entries in its internal field state), so they are either silently ignored — making the design's claim that React Hook Form touched/dirty state is supplied to Field.Root dead code — or, if Field.Root spreads unknown props onto its rendered div, they leak to the DOM as invalid attributes and trigger React unknown-prop warnings.
findings.evidence: form.tsx hunk: `<Field.Root ref={ref} name={name} invalid={invalid} touched={isTouched} dirty={isDirty} ...>`; design.md states 'Supply `name`, `invalid`, `touched`, and `dirty` from `getFieldState`' as the mechanism for Field/RHF state agreement. Base UI's Field.Root accepts `invalid`/`name`/`validate`/`validationMode` as external inputs but derives `touched`/`dirty` internally from control interactions.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `touched={isTouched}` and `dirty={isDirty}` (Base UI tracks them from control events), or verify against the installed @base-ui/react types that they are accepted and meaningful; update design.md to match reality.

findings.claim: None of the ten assistant-ui `asChild` → `render` migrations has any runtime test: the new test files only cover Button, BreadcrumbLink, Sidebar, and Select, so the delta-spec scenario 'An action primitive renders a local button … merges its behavior onto that render element without adding a wrapper element' is unverified, and verification.md's claim of '7/7 scenarios covered' is inaccurate.
findings.evidence: composition-patterns.test.tsx imports only from `@/components/ui/{breadcrumb,button,select,sidebar}` — nothing mounts `ThreadPrimitive.ScrollToBottom`, `ComposerPrimitive.Send/Cancel`, `ActionBarPrimitive.*`, or `BranchPickerPrimitive.*`. spec.md scenario requires merged behavior with no added wrapper; verification.md 'Correctness' section cites only the ui/ composition test and the form test as interaction evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a focused render test for at least the representative primitives (e.g. ComposerPrimitive.Send and ActionBarPrimitive.Copy) asserting the TooltipIconButton/Button element receives the primitive's onClick/disabled and that children render inside the render element.

findings.claim: `FormItem` now calls `useFormFieldState()`, which throws when there is no `FormFieldContext` and requires an RHF `FormProvider`; previously FormItem rendered a plain div with only a generated id and worked standalone, so any existing or future standalone use of `FormItem` now crashes at render.
findings.evidence: form.tsx hunk: `const { name, invalid, isTouched, isDirty } = useFormFieldState()` added inside FormItem, and `useFormFieldState` throws `new Error("useFormField should be used within <FormField>")` when `!fieldContext` and calls `useFormContext()` unconditionally. Pre-diff FormItem body was only `const id = React.useId()` + `<div>`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document the tightened contract explicitly, or make FormItem tolerate a missing field context (e.g. only pass name/invalid/touched/dirty when context exists).

findings.claim: Splitting `useFormFieldState` into FormItem means every FormItem now subscribes to `formState` via `getFieldState(name, formState)`, so invalid/touched/dirty transitions re-render the entire field subtree where previously FormItem was render-stable.
findings.evidence: form.tsx hunk: FormItem body gained `useFormFieldState()` which reads `getFieldState(fieldContext.name, formState)`; pre-diff only FormLabel/FormControl/FormMessage subscribed via `useFormField`.
findings.suggested_fix: Acceptable if intentional, but consider reading state via a narrower subscription or noting the re-render cost in design.md risks.

findings.claim: `match={Boolean(body)}` on `Field.Error` is dead logic: the early `if (!body) return null` above guarantees `body` is truthy at this point, so `match` is always `true` and conveys nothing.
findings.evidence: form.tsx hunk retains `const body = error ? ... : children` / `if (!body) { return null }` context and adds `match={Boolean(body)}` to Field.Error.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `match` (i.e. `match={true}`) or drop the prop if Base UI's default rendering already handles presence; alternatively remove the early return and let `match={Boolean(body)}` do the gating, but not both.

findings.claim: FormLabel now inlines a copy of the Label component's class string instead of composing the existing `Label`, creating a styling fork that will drift if label.tsx is restyled.
findings.evidence: form.tsx hunk removes `import { Label } from "@/components/ui/label"` and hardcodes `"flex items-center gap-2 text-sm leading-none font-medium select-none group-data-[disabled=true]:..."` into FormLabel's className.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the shared label class string (e.g. export `labelVariants` from label.tsx) and reuse it in FormLabel.
